chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah said:

I asked him about a traveler who arrived at his family before the sun's declination (midday), and he had already eaten. He said: 'It is not appropriate for him to eat anything that day, nor to have intercourse during the month of Ramadan, if he has a wife.'

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: His family (specifically wife in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who arrives home before midday during Ramadan after eating?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Sama'a, the Imam clarifies that a traveler who breaks his fast before solar noon (zawal) must continue abstaining from food and sexual intercourse for the remainder of that day, effectively treating the rest of the day as a continuation of his fasted state. This ruling highlights the distinction between the obligation of making up the day (qada) and the immediate prohibition of acts that break the fast once the traveler has already consumed something, emphasizing the continuity of the fasting discipline even after the initial breaking point. The prohibition on sexual intercourse extends for the entire month, reflecting the severity of the missed fast in the sacred month of Ramadan.
